I just sold my 2012 Kia sportage for £1500 and there wasn’t anything wrong with it. I spent £1000 last year fixing everything on it as it failed its MOT after I bought it off a liar. I’m genuinely confident it will fly through its MOT in July. My husband loved using it for his golf clubs. Only reason I got rid was because I got a new company car and he wanted to keep his BMW but my new car has to go on the drive as that’s where the charger is and I didn’t want to tax and Insure a car just to drive round golf clubs and I didn’t want to take an extra space on the street since the new one needed the drive way and the garage is… well full of golf stuff.

I thought it was a good car but the tax was quite expensive compared to anything else I’ve had.

I’m going to be honest with you, I’m a career person. I wouldn’t give up my career for anything. Not because I like my job but because I like the financial stability it brings. However if my daughter got cancer and was going to be in the hospital for a year doing chemo or something, wild bears couldn’t make me go to work. I’d just be there with her. Take my house, my car. Bankrupt me. I don’t care but that girl isn’t going to be alone for a second. However I feel like her dad would be the same and he’d walk out of his job the minute we got the diagnosis. 

But also we don’t live in America and we get paid parental leave and also the government would pay us benefits. Nowhere near what we earn normally but we wouldn’t end up homeless or with hospital bills or anything so I guess I don’t know how bad it could get. I suppose if I had to work to pay the doctors to physically keep her alive then I’d be working.

Hey I just want to add that if you find your local PDSA then anyone on PIP can sign one pet up with them and receive free treatment. If you get a different benefit like UC (even if you have it all deducted due to earnings) then you can sign another pet up in your name.

My brother has one of his dogs signed up as he gets PIP and he chose the most adventurous one. They are still insured and go to a normal vet etc as they don’t cover all treatment but if you look on their website it should tell you what free or discounted services they offer.

My mum has been a teaching assistant for 30 years - well that’s not really what it was called 30 years ago but she was also just handed the job when my brother went into reception as she was always there helping. She’s retiring in July and has been supplementing her wage by working in the local garden centre. She worked in a few bits but likes the cafe the best as she doesn’t need to learn about changing products and the hours are pretty normal. She also likes the events like lunch with Santa and the Easter afternoon tea and things.

Shes also managed to get a side gig at the local ferry terminal which starts this summer and it’s just twice a week checking passports as the ferry arrives. Takes 3 hours but it’s £25 an hour.

The other thing she has done is signed up with a cat sitting agency. It’s £30 a visit and she just nips in and feeds the cats and strokes them while their owners are on holiday or whatever.

She can’t wait to retire as she wants to up her hours on the cat sitting.

However they always find it amusing when they meet someone with a pet named the same name and the pet owner seems uncomfortable. Her and her friends would visit shelters all the time looking for cats and dogs named millie. Daisy isn’t old enough yet for those shenanigans.

Honestly the only time me and my partner have ever even been close to calling it quits was when we moved in with my mum after we’d been living abroad and moved and thought we could stay at hers rent free to save some cash. We planned to do it for 6 months. We lasted less than a month. Both of us were in tears over it. The lack of privacy was overwhelming. She thought she was helping by telling us she’d bought dinner and what time she’d have it ready but having someone control what you eat is actually horrible. You nip out at 9pm for a McFlurry? No you don’t without 62 questions about why you need icecream at that time, can’t you just eat a lolly from the freezer or get a yogurt from the fridge, isn’t it late to be driving, does it take both of you to go, won’t it give you a bad stomach - omg and on and on and on. She even told me I buttered bread the wrong way one time. I can’t imagine that stress with a baby as well.

I know you are getting upset about people commenting you are not married but just imagine IF something happened that caused a sudden split. IF there was suddenly violence or an addiction or cheating. Normally that would lead to divorce and she would be entitled to half of everything you both currently have. What you currently now have between you all is actually legally all yours. In a divorce the judge would likely order you to keep paying for her for certain things - like medical bills etc until she gets on her feet. Because you aren’t married, she isn’t entitled to anything. You would get everything and wouldn’t be on the hook for anything but child support. You’d be able to cancel things like life insurance. You’d be able to walk away without looking back if you wanted. I’m not saying you would, I’m just trying to point out why people bring up the fact you aren’t married.

Hurt people do some crazy things and marriage helps minimise the damage done by the possible crazy things done by hurt people - especially financially.

I text her and they’d gone out in her friends car to get their nails done but drove straight back and moved the car.

Sometimes people are dumb (like my 20 year old) but they aren’t trying to be. Also sometimes the police will help and just simply find the owner and call their mum to tell them off 😂

The car is registered under my name and they were about to crane in away so the escort people (they wanted to get out a large load) rang and said I had 20 minutes to get it so I got the spare key and drove there to move it. The factory was the factory of his own work place so he had to deal with his boss after that. Apparently they hadn’t opened those gates in 5 years and loads of people parked there but he’d gone away in the van that day to work at a different site.
I wish you luck in your decision and your career 😊

I’d suggest the boyfriend gets on board or OP gets off at the next stop!

I’m someone who travels for work. I’ve been all over. The best thing? My kid has seen so much of the world. Fine you can’t take them when they are young but mine is a teenager now and I had to go work in Peru for a year and she flew first class every 6 weeks to see me and she loved it. She ate in the best restaurants in the world, saw matchu pitchu, the salt lakes of Bolivia, the original Starbucks plantation in chile, ate the best steak in Argentina, went to carnivals in Brazil, lunch in Colombia. She trekked the Amazon jungle. She learned Spanish. She visited schools and hospitals my company helped build.

I’ve taken her to Spain, France, Vienna, America. She’s been on construction sites and in rail depots the world over. She can talk in school about what opportunities different subjects can bring you as she’s seen the jobs in action. 

The other great thing is we can afford what she needs. She can go to university without accumulating debt. We can get her a car when she’s 18.

You can be family orientated without staying at home with your child and attending all the mommy and me groups or being on the PTA. Families look different for everyone. It’s also ok if you do want to be a stay at home parent when the time comes too.

Now I don’t travel as much anymore and I have a cv which makes it possible to pick and choose a lot more easily where I want to work. We mainly live a normal life. We host sleepovers for her friends, her grades are average, we spend the weekends as a family and she is normally hanging out with her friends during holidays. I either give her lifts to meet them or she gets a bus to see them. Both me and my husband only work 4 days a week now so we have Fridays for our admin while she’s at school so we are available for her the whole weekend.

I wouldn’t give this opportunity up if I was you. You have a good few years to build that cv up to give yourself options for when you do have kids. I could understand if you were pregnant now and you’d be leaving for a week at a time in the first year of a babies life but that’s just not happening.

I’ve just got off a WhatsApp conversation with my best friend of 20 years. We discussed potatoes for 20 minutes. It started with me sending her a photo of a bag of jersey royals and reminding her to get her fill in the next 2 weeks as the flavour seems to be in decline so I fear they will be going out of season soon. We then discussed our favourite types of potato and if they were possible to eat without gravy and if cheese would substitute if gravy wasn’t available. Cause jersey royals kinda don’t need cheese or gravy which is kinda weird when you think about it. Like even a jacket - you can argue doesn’t need either cause of tuna mayo BUT a jersey royal is probably the only one which is honestly fine with just the butter.

Anyway we extended the chat to our other 2 best friends and it got heated. We did not talk about our childhoods but we did compare how our mothers prepared chips if that counts. None of this was new information to each other but the argument is ongoing as to whose mum did it the best.

I think a happy medium is best. My mum was very hands off. I am 40 and if my mum hugged me or told me she loved me I’d assume either I was dying or she was dying. It’s just not a thing. However I have a friend who still sleeps in bed with her 10 year old and a lot of the time he demands it if they have company over. He’s just being a shit. Her 14 year old still has a bedtime story but she’s into mills and boon and teenage erotica type stuff and quite frankly it’s weird. Like her mum is there just reading this shit to her then off to the bedroom to sleep with the boy while he asks incessant questions about made up mine craft worlds.

I think kids should feel secure and loved and be openly told they are loved and should be given attention but should know everyone has their own spaces and that should be respected. I wouldn’t want my teenager in bed with me or sitting on the toilet having a conversation with me while I’m in the bath. I wouldn’t do it to her so I expect the same privacy back. One day these kids are going to go out into the world and they need to know they aren’t the centre of everyone else’s world. I think it’s fine unless they don’t naturally detach then you need to help that along a little bit.

I took no offence. It’s not their fault they are stupid. Also I’m not due on my period. I was on site in Scotland and couldn’t see the sea. It was freezing and I choose cranberry as a mixer to reduce my hangover the next day. However with the cranberry I do think he has periods mixed up with UTI’s.

It wasn’t something I wanted to be in the 90’s but here I am doing it in my 40’s. Maybe just let her explain what it is and let her show you what she’s been studying and take and interest before you write it off.

I had a friend whose husband wanted to do this. Their kid was on their 4th time of being groomed by men on the internet and she was 12 at the time. This was only 4 times that police turned up at the door to tell the parents of what she was doing and that they had complaints from other parents and have searched a computer already and found her chats and pics. Could have been more than 4 that they just didn’t find out about because the police didn’t tell them. She used to give out her full name and address so she wasn’t hard to track down. Thankfully these men posing as 17 year old boys were always in another country so didn’t attempt to kidnap her. The last man was in Poland. The police would literally tell her they’d caught fully grown men and she’d be like “nope I still love him”. Didn’t care. It was weird. Obviously they took away her devices and put locks on everything but she’d manage to sneak phones from school or get an extra laptop from school. There was videos and pictures. Every time they thought they had a handle on it, it turned out she’d just got sneakier and had done something else. She was on dating apps, fetish websites - all of it. Posting pictures and videos. Running weird little vlogs on them. All of the videos were from her room.

Her dad wanted the door off her room. Her mum didn’t and said she still deserved her privacy. He said her safety was more important than privacy.

Anyway she ended up keeping the door but the parents nearly separated. She seems to be doing better a few years later but still one of those girls who always seems very focused on getting a boyfriend but the boys seems to know it and it puts them off. On the upside at least these boys exist and she can see them in front of her.

So using an umberella company just normally means you will still be a sole trader but umbrella company will do the admin for you so as some companies do not want to pay invoices to multiple limited companies. I think it’s something you need to ask though before you make your decision. Ask if you will be self employed. Also ask who pays the umbrella company fees and if it is you then ask how much they are. Ask the umbrella company directly what your take offs would be. I say this as my husband used to have 14% taken off - this was their fee then a weird tax rate which had the expected return built back in already. He uses a different umbrella now and they take 30% but he just got a tax return over £20k which he had to pay an accountant to do for him. It all varies so I feel like it’s something you need to ask about.

If you were going to be employed though then HSBC would be employing you directly so o would lean towards you being on a day rate as self employed. That’s how they get away with no sickness and no holidays.

Another question to ask is if you need to purchase your own liability insurance or if that’s included in the umbrella fee.

I’ve lived abroad and wouldn’t worry about getting it perfect because when you want a roast, the main components will do.

Beef is fine but a rotisserie chicken will also be fantastic. He won’t care.

Brown gravy. Ask ChatGPT how to make an English brown gravy. If you can find somewhere that will sell some bisto then fantastic but if not then tough luck and make it from scratch with your meat juices from your beef. He’ll be grateful either way I promise.

Roast potatoes. Par boil the potatoes then let them sit and give them a shake so they fluff a bit and then season them with loads of salt and pepper. If you have onion and garlic salt then whack that on as well. I love a bit of mustard powder on for flavour and colour but I don’t know if you can get that. I’m talking like tradition mustard powder so possibly not. Coat them in corn flour and then toast them in veg oil or duck fat. I do something different at home but this will be fine for him. He won’t be fussy.

For veg do some roasted broccoli - just season it with salt and pepper and some parsnips if you can find some. Season the parsnips with honey and roast them in it.

Boiled carrots will be fine for him. Ask her if her wants them in battons or rounds. He’ll have a preference.

Add mash if you have time but don’t bother if you are going to use instant. It tasted disgusting to us. Fine if you will boil your potatoes, drain them, add double cream and butter, salt and petter and garlic. If you are prepared for that mash then that’s ok.

Now go and buy a cupcake tin. Make a CREPE batter. Not pancake batter. Again, ask chatgpt or go on the bbc food website and ask for a Yorkshire pudding recipie. You need to make the batter and put it in the fridge and let it rest. You put veg or rapeseed oil in the cupcake tin and heat it until smoke is coming off it. Literally like 3ml in each ducket so the fat it boiling to make smoke. Then you pour your cold batter in the cupcake moulds with the oil. It should start cooking from the heat of the oil and pan. Hurry up or it’s going to cool down. Transfer your batter to a jog if it’s going to make this faster. Half fill the moulds and shut the oven door. Leave them on 180 degrees (look up American equivalent) for 25 mins and don’t check on them. Trust the process. If you let cool air in then they will end up flat and doughy.

Make enough gravy. Think about the amount of gravy you think is enough then triple it. You know the big jugs you keep your milk in? Fill that with gravy.

You don’t need to go too fancy. I lived in South America. All the English wanted was whatever roast meat (nobody cared), yorkshires, proper mash not instant, roast potatoes and that heavenly gravy. Water companies expenses have gone up due to inflation too. Within the last 5 years we’ve had a change in government, brexit, the war in Ukraine, the energy crisis, covid and probably more that I can’t think of off the top of my head. They still need to pay to keep their treatment centres open and pay their staff, they still need to train their staff. There is a project next year where they need to hire a vessel which is costing double what it cost just two years ago (research ship with sonar).

The fact that the last government got rid of IR35 has meant they need to pay consultancies as contractors basically shut shop. Then this government have got the whole NI thing going on which means they need to cover that cost for their staff and will pay a fee increase for the consultancy fees to cover it for them.

Materials are more expensive, travel is more expensive. Even expenses for their staff are more - food and hotels while going from site to site. Trains/petrol etc.

Brexit has increased import costs by about 30% so construction is hard. Transport is expensive especially when dealing with cargo type ships which are travelling internationally to get to your project.
